Holding Suzlon? Don't buy more before you see this. Multibagger, or trap?
Fifty six lakh Indians own it. In 2008, it touched four hundred and sixty rupees. Then debt crushed it. By 2023, it was eight rupees.
Today it's near thirty seven. Forty percent below last year's high of sixty one. So what does Suzlon actually do?
It makes wind turbines, the giant fans that turn wind into electricity. Built in fifteen factory hubs, across Gujarat, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
It also services over nine thousand six hundred turbines. And its machines spin in seventeen countries, from the US to Australia to Germany.
Today's results. Revenue up twenty six percent. A record seven hundred ten megawatts delivered. And an order book above six gigawatts.
But profit fell sixty nine percent. Don't panic. Last year had a one time tax gain. Without it, profit grew just one percent, and margins slipped.
So, multibagger or trap? Neither, yet. Debt is almost gone, and profit is real. But promoters own only eleven point seven percent, and growth just slowed.
